subject: Request: transitional coverage affirmation to close post-report gap
messages:
From: Helen Cross <helen.cross@lumenware.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumenware.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transitional coverage request for vendor SOC 2 window

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. LumenWare’s procurement team is wrapping up our vendor security review and we have a remaining ask around the audit reporting window. Our current review requires documentation to cover the period from 2026-07-01 to the contract effective date (we’re targeting 2026-10-15). Your SOC 2 Type II report covers through 2026-06-30.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide a transitional coverage statement (bridge letter) that: 
- Affirms there have been no material changes to controls relevant to security and availability since 2026-06-30, and
- Identifies any exceptions (if present) and mitigation actions with dates.

Our legal team also asked whether the letter needs to be signed by your auditor (KPMG) or if a company-signed affirmation is sufficient for procurement. If auditor confirmation is required, please indicate the expected lead time.

I’ve CC’d our procurement mailbox; they’ll attach the vendor questionnaire and timelines. We’d appreciate a preliminary response by end of day Friday so we can keep our review on schedule.

Thanks,
Helen Cross
Vendor Risk Manager
LumenWare

Attachments: vendor_qs_LumenWare_v2.xlsx (referenced)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helen Cross <helen.cross@lumenware.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenware.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transitional coverage request for vendor SOC 2 window

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear note and the timeline. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a transitional coverage (bridge) letter; a company-signed affirmation is usually acceptable for procurement in most cases. If LumenWare requires auditor attestation, we will coordinate but that typically takes 2–3 weeks depending on auditor availability.

Next steps we suggest: 
1) We’ll draft a concise transitional coverage affirmation that: confirms the SOC 2 report period (ending 2026-06-30), states no material changes to security/availability controls, and lists any control exceptions with remediation dates. 
2) Redwood legal/security will review the draft and provide a version for signature. 
3) If LumenWare needs auditor confirmation, please flag that explicitly; we’ll loop in KPMG and provide a timeline.

I’m looping in Rishi (Security & Trust) for control detail and Naomi (Compliance) for audit coordination. Rishi/Naomi — Helen’s team prefers a draft by Friday EOD (their procurement cadence). Can we aim to produce a draft transitional cover letter and include the redacted SOC 2 PDF and a short evidence checklist?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_Redacted_2026-06-30.pdf (prepared)

From: Helen Cross <helen.cross@lumenware.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumenware.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transitional coverage request for vendor SOC 2 window

Thanks Kimberly — that timeline works for us. Procurement has flagged that if there are any open exceptions they must be called out with expected completion windows. Auditor sign-off is not mandatory but preferred; if you can indicate whether KPMG would be willing to provide a short confirmation email that would be ideal.

Also, procurement just added one ask: could you include a simple one-page controls summary (high level) that maps the report’s common criteria to the Redwood hosted environment? That will speed internal review.

If you send the draft to procurement@lumenware.com and copy me, I’ll route it to legal and security reviewers.

Best,
Helen

Attachments: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helen Cross <helen.cross@lumenware.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenware.com>, Alex Brewer <alex.brewer@kpmg.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transitional coverage request for vendor SOC 2 window

Hi Helen — attaching our draft transitional coverage affirmation and a one-page controls map for your review. Key points included in the draft: 
- Report covered period: 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30 (Type II).
- Statement: no material changes to security/availability controls affecting the scope since report end date, except where noted.
- Exceptions: none open as of 2026-09-28. (We list closed items and remediation dates in the appendix.)
- Auditor confirmation: KPMG has indicated they can provide a short confirmation email on request; lead time ~10 business days.

Please review the attached documents and let us know whether the company-signed affirmation suffices or if you want us to request auditor confirmation. If procurement needs a signature authority, I can route the DocuSign envelope to our VP of Security once you confirm the final text.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: transitional_coverage_template.docx (draft), controls_map_onepage.pdf (summary), kpmg_confirmation_request.eml (sent to auditor)
